weeks.quote: God is making a family out of strangers. So we love it. We guard it. We praise him for it.

devotionals.title: Saved to a Family
devotionals.scripture_text: So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints, and members of God's household.
devotionals.reflection:
Most of us know that God saves us from something. Sin. Death. Hell. But here's the thing: that is only half of the good news. When God saves us, He saves us to something. He saves us to a family.

Think about what that does to how you walk into church. You are not a visitor who happens to share a room with strangers. You are a member of a household. The people around you did not end up there by accident, and neither did you.

Loneliness is not mainly about being alone. It is about not being known. God's answer is not a program or a pep talk. It is a people. He takes strangers, people who share nothing except Jesus, and He makes them family.

That is why Paul closed the book of Romans with a long list of names. They were not an audience. They were his family.

I want you to start this week by believing it. You belong. You were not saved to sit alone. You were saved to be home.
devotionals.question: Where have you been treating church like a room you visit instead of a family you belong to?
devotionals.prayer: Father, thank You that You did not save me just to rescue me, but to bring me home. Thank You for the people You have placed around me, even the ones I barely know. Help me believe that I belong, and help me welcome someone else like family. In Jesus' name, amen.

devotionals.title: Friendly Is Not Family
devotionals.scripture_text: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
devotionals.reflection:
It is easy to be friendly. We shake hands. We say it is good to see you. We ask how the week went and accept "fine" for an answer. But friendly is not the same as family. A family knows what is behind the "fine."

So how are we supposed to weep with those who weep if we do not know who is weeping? How do we rejoice with those who rejoice if nobody ever hears the good news? We cannot. Not without knowing each other.

The people you sit near every Sunday have real stories. Real heartaches. Real troubles. Real blessings. They are not background. They are people God put in your path.

Someone has to take the first step, and I want you to see that it might be you. Send the text. Ask the second question. Stay a few minutes after the service.

It may take some chipping away. It may take time and effort. But God called you into a family for exactly this reason, so you would not have to live alone.
devotionals.question: Who is one person at church you could text today to ask how they are really doing?
devotionals.prayer: Lord, forgive me for settling for friendly when You have called me to family. Give me real affection for the people around me. Show me who needs a text, a question, or a seat beside me this week. Help me take the first step. In Jesus' name, amen.

devotionals.title: Watch Who You Listen To
devotionals.scripture_text: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles contrary to the teaching that you learned. Avoid them, because such people do not serve our Lord Christ but their own appetites. They deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting with smooth talk and flattering words.
devotionals.reflection:
Paul spends the first part of Romans 16 greeting the family, and then he stops to warn them. Why? Because the enemy wants nothing more than to destroy a family. Division causes pain, heartache, and church hurt. If you have felt that, you know it is real.

Here is how it usually comes. Not as a villain, but as a smooth talker. The words sound reasonable. They feel good to hear. They may even come from someone holding a Bible. But Paul says they serve their own appetites, not Christ.

So what do we do? Not panic, but pay attention. Be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil. Measure everything against Scripture, not opinions, not emotions, and not whoever sounds the most convincing. If someone contradicts what the church has held for two thousand years, be careful.

And learn it in community. Trying to figure out God by yourself is a recipe for trouble. You were never meant to guard the family alone.

I want you to ask one question this week about every voice you listen to: does this line up with the Word?
devotionals.question: Which voice do you listen to most, and how do you check what it says against Scripture?
devotionals.prayer: Father, thank You for gathering me into a family that You also guard. Give me wisdom to know what is good and a clear eye for what is not. Help me love Your Word enough to know it, and keep me close to Your people when I am tempted to walk alone. In Jesus' name, amen.

devotionals.title: Warriors, Not Heroes
devotionals.scripture_text: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who have worked hard in the Lord.
devotionals.reflection:
We know almost nothing about Tryphaena and Tryphosa. Their names probably mean dainty and delicate, and they were probably twins. Paul's only comment about them is that they worked hard in the Lord. That is it. One line, and it made the last chapter of Romans.

Think about the difference between a hero and a warrior. Heroes want the glory for themselves. Warriors want the glory for one another. They know they are fighting for something bigger than themselves.

Most of us will never be famous. Most of us will be forgotten within a few generations. But here is the good news: obscurity in the eyes of people is never irrelevance in the eyes of God. He will not forget your name. He will not forget what you did in His name, even if nobody else noticed.

Today is Thanksgiving, so here is a way to say thanks that counts. Thank someone who works where no one is watching. The person who sets up the chairs, makes the coffee, or prays for you without telling you.

Say it out loud. Tell them God sees it too.
devotionals.question: Who serves your church in ways almost no one sees, and how could you thank them this week?
devotionals.prayer: Lord, thank You that You see what no one else sees. Forgive me for wanting credit when I should want Your glory. Make me a warrior who serves gladly and encourages others. Help me thank the quiet workers in my life. In Jesus' name, amen.

devotionals.title: He Is Able
devotionals.scripture_text: Now to him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation about Jesus Christ...
devotionals.reflection:
Paul finishes this whole letter with praise. Fifteen chapters of sin, grace, faith, and the power of the gospel end in one declaration: God is able to strengthen you. Not you, holding yourself together. God, holding you.

I want you to stop trying to hold yourself up. When you feel like you are failing, when you feel like you are struggling, look back and say, "God, I am not the one who holds me. You do."

Here is why you can rest. Your salvation does not rest on you. You did not earn it, and you cannot lose it. It is a gift of grace from a holy God, established and sustained through Jesus. The same gospel that saved you is the gospel that keeps you.

And you do not carry this alone. God is making a family out of strangers. So we love it, we guard it, and we praise Him for it.

This week, when you run out of strength, pray the verse back to Him: "You are able to strengthen me."
devotionals.question: Where are you trying to hold yourself up right now, and what would it look like to hand that to the God who is able?
devotionals.prayer: Father, I praise You because You are able. I confess that I try to hold myself together, and I am tired. Strengthen me by Your gospel and keep me in the family You have gathered. Thank You that my salvation rests on Jesus, not on me. To You be the glory forever. In Jesus' name, amen.

weeks.opening_question: Who was the first person who made you feel welcome the first time you walked into a church or a new group?
questions: The sermon said loneliness is not about being alone, it is about not being in relationship. When have you felt lonely in a room full of people, and what would have changed that?

We can be friendly without being family. Think of someone who sits near you most Sundays. What do you actually know about their story, and what is one step you could take this month to know them better?

Paul names people by who they belong to, not by their resumes, and we know almost nothing about most of them. Where are you tempted to want credit for your serving, and what would it look like to serve as a warrior rather than a hero?
Paul warns us to watch out for people who use smooth talk and flattering words. What is one voice you listen to regularly, and how do you check what it teaches against Scripture?
The sermon asked us to stop trying to hold ourselves up. Where do you feel like you have to hold yourself together right now, and what would it look like to pray Romans 16:25 back to God this week?

pray.heading: Make room to pray
pray.intro: Prayer grows a life with God, and it usually starts small. Here are two tools. They are tools, not requirements, and there are many others.

items.name: Echo Prayer
items.description: Keep a list of the people and needs you're praying for, set reminders, and mark prayers answered so you can see what God has done. Follow our church's prayer feed in the app. Available on iPhone and Android.

items.name: Pause
items.description: Free guided pauses of 1, 3, 5 or 10 minutes, read by author John Eldredge, for stopping in the middle of a busy day and handing it back to God. One tool among many. Available on iPhone and Android.
